title: Angular and RxJS Integration knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Angular and RxJS Integration”?
options: Angular and RxJS Integration should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Angular and RxJS Integration helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Angular and RxJS Integration means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Angular and RxJS Integration removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
questions.answer_key: Angular and RxJS Integration helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Angular and RxJS Integration is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Observables in templates” in this lesson?
options: Connect “Observables in templates” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “Observables in templates” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Observables in templates” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Observables in templates” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Observables in templates” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Observables in templates” under Angular and RxJS Integration. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Angular and RxJS Integration”?
options: Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
